question: Which Linux companion app architecture and ownership model should OpenClaw sponsor now that the Windows side is shipped through Windows Hub?
rationale: The open Linux candidates touch native UI, gateway auth, local system integration, and packaging, so automation cannot choose the project’s long-term desktop architecture or security bar safely.

options.title: Adopt one GTK-native Linux track
options.body: Choose either the C/GTK or Rust/GTK candidate as the sponsored core path, require security/packaging proof, and close or redirect competing tracks.

options.title: Keep Linux app external for now
options.body: Leave the core repo terminal/browser-first on Linux and direct companion app experiments to external repos until ownership and packaging are settled.

options.title: Split the umbrella into narrower Linux milestones
options.body: Keep this issue as strategy only and create separate app-shell, packaging, notifications, node-capability, and dashboard-hosting follow-ups.

recommendation.title: Adopt one GTK-native Linux track
recommendation.body: Choose either the C/GTK or Rust/GTK candidate as the sponsored core path, require security/packaging proof, and close or redirect competing tracks.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete opened the issue, set the GTK-native direction in discussion, and recently maintained the platform app docs and Windows release promotion surface.
